content.title: About
content.content: Key lime pie is a dessert consisting of a buttery crust, creamy filling, and tangy lime juice. The lime provides a bright aroma and refreshing tartness, balanced by a sweet base.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lime is a staple in Caribbean cuisine, where the original key lime pie originated.
The classic recipe uses lime juice and zest, egg yolks, sweetened condensed milk, and butter.
Key lime pie is often served chilled to enhance its refreshing character.
In the United States the pie gained popularity in the 1920s as tropical flavors became fashionable.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Lime is rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids in lime help combat free radicals and may promote heart health.

items.title: Lower Calorie Content
items.content: Compared with many desserts, key lime pie can be lower in calories when sugar is used moderately.

items.title: Citrus Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lime.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity of lime can irritate sensitive teeth or the stomach if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pie chilled, cutting it into individual slices. It can be garnished with whipped cream, berries, or mint for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the pie refrigerated, covered with plastic wrap or in an airtight container, for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze individual portions wrapped in foil and placed in a freezer bag.
